newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH UTILITY SME SEES LOWER 96 NET PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH UTILITY SME SEES LOWER 96 NET PROFIT.

text.p: Czech electrical utility Severomoravksa Energetika a.s. (SME) on Friday said it expects its 1996 net profit to ease to about 500 million crowns from 591 million the previous year.
SME Finance Director Frantisek Korinek told Reuters the final profit figure will be influenced mainly by the final price the firm will have to pay eletricity generator CEZ a.s. for electricity.
The price is to be determined by the Finance Ministry in February.

CEZ and the country's regional distributors have been locked in a dispute over what price should be paid for electricity supplies, and who is responsible for losses along lines and at transforming stations.
In 1995, SME posted a net profit of 591 million crowns on revenues of 13.1 billion. Korinek added that SME's 1996 revenues should total 14.2 billion crowns.
The firm is expected to pay a 40 crown per share dividend for 1996, after paying a 30 crown divdend in 1995.
